title: XGD — AI writes it. XGD keeps it working.

seoMeta.title: XGD — AI writes it. XGD keeps it working.
seoMeta.description: XGD maintains a living spec of your software's intended behavior and tests the running system against it on every change. You own that intent and the architecture; XGD owns the implementation.

config.successMessage: You’re on the list — we’ll be in touch.

children.text: Work at conversational speed. Behind you, XGD maintains a living spec of what your software should do, tests the running system against it on every change, and repairs what breaks. You keep product, architecture and quality.

An agent can produce a thousand lines before lunch. What it cannot tell you is whether the ninety thousand it wrote last month still do what you promised. So you reach for discipline — specs first, a review on every diff, a full cycle per change — and a two-minute question becomes an afternoon.
Every change can break something that already worked. With no record of what was intended, nothing can tell you whether a behaviour moved by design or by accident.
Specs up front, a diff to review, a full generated cycle for a one-line fix. All of it correct, and all of it sitting between you and the result.
A process you skip protects nothing. The only governance that counts is the kind that survives contact with a real working day.
You keep working. XGD reconciles behind you.

You work with the AI the way you already do — ask, see it run, adjust. In the background, XGD folds what you built into a capability matrix: a traceable chain from what your software is for down to executable proof that it still does it. Nothing waits on it.
Interactive, at conversational cadence. An intent ticket is opened, tests are written, the commit carries its traceability. Five to ten minutes, not an afternoon.
In the background, the change is folded into the matrix — capability, story, acceptance criteria, and an executable test for each. You are never waiting on this.
Every criterion is pinned by a test that runs against the live system. A specification document drifts silently; this one fails the moment the code stops matching it.

Free coding on a complex codebase throws roughly one regression for every two tickets — that is the going rate for the practice, not a fault of the tool. XGD catches them against the recorded intent, and fixes them.

Nine months, one person: 130,000 lines of production code and 300,000 lines of tests, not one line of it read by a human. We built the fully autonomous version first — then noticed we were avoiding it, because waiting hours for a small change cost more than it saved. Free coding exists because of what we found out about ourselves.
“I built a platform I’ve never read the source of — but I never stopped being its engineer.”
You’re out of the code. Not out of the project.
The split is deliberate and it does not move. You are out of the coding loop — not writing it, not reading it, not reviewing diffs. Everywhere else, you are still the engineer.

XGD does not claim your software is correct. It guarantees that every claim of correctness is backed by inspectable evidence — and that every gap in that evidence is visible rather than quietly absent.
The beta opens when the system is stable, not before — leave your email and we’ll tell you the moment it does. Tell us what you’re building if you’d like a reply.
